svg.text: Offline document ingestion and real-time, role-scoped retrieval — traced through the actual application agents.
Documents receive access metadata before indexing
roles_mapping assigns filenames to document-role tags; role_permissions later maps verified JWT roles to those tags.
Ingestion builds a replacement index, checks the result, then moves the live alias; the previous index is retained for rollback.
Non-dry-run ingestion stores original files in MinIO before extraction.
Authentication happens once at connection; expiry is checked again per query
Signed identity and permissions travel with every query
LLM classifies intent from configured taxonomy.
This is conversational routing, not RBAC.
Reads STM + relevant LTM under memory_scope_id.
Uses context only to resolve follow-up wording.
Both keyed by user + permission scope
If permissions are empty, fail closed.
RRF merges BM25 and vector candidates.
Cross-encoder scores relevance; keep top chunks.
Low relevance → fixed role-safe message; retrieval errors get a service message.
Only accepted authorized chunks enter context.
Grounded answer with filename citations; no outside knowledge.
The reply is correlated to the original WebSocket connection
Authentication decides who the caller is; RBAC supplies allowed document roles; Elasticsearch filters both retrieval modes before synthesis.
Cache hits skip retrieval and synthesis; checkpoints resume interrupted request runs
Redis TTL (15 min default); same permission scope
Thread key: retrieval-{request_id}; persist graph state between nodes.
On redelivery: resume the saved next step, or reuse a completed result.
Checkpoint TTL defaults to 1,440 minutes; Redis Stack RediSearch is required.
Signed request carries a stable request_id used by the checkpoint thread.
Commit the input offset only after successful response handling.
Failure leaves the offset uncommitted so retry can recover saved graph state.
Cache keys include the authorization scope; personal-memory follow-ups bypass shared caching.
